title: Stazione Zoologica Napoli microscopic preparations: 1882–1884 dealer-network upgrade

already_closed.catalogue: 1880/1881 Naples price list offers 423 microscopic preparations as numbered products.
already_closed.object_example: St Andrews BPM/1/T8/6 closes surviving Naples object ↔ catalogue offering 383 (Delphinus phocaena — Penis), with Panis/Penis transcription guard.
already_closed.claim_level: S/A++ for catalogue-offering identity; individual-copy shipment history remains open.

primary_report_locator.title: Bericht über die Zoologische Station während der Jahre 1882-1884
primary_report_locator.container: Mittheilungen aus der Zoologischen Station zu Neapel, Bd. 6
primary_report_locator.verification_state: The primary report and page range are located, but the dealer-sales table/text on pp. 130-131 has not yet been independently transcribed from the BHL page images in this pass.

secondary_extraction_pending_primary_ver.source: Brian Stevenson, 'Stazione Zoologica Napoli / Fritz Meyer', Microscopist.net, citing Mittheilungen 1886, vol. 6, pp. 130-131

claims.claim: The Station sold 225 microscope slides to Edmund Wheeler in February 1882.
The 1882-1884 sales list includes Edmund Wheeler, R. & J. Beck (London), Edward Ward (Manchester), Gustav Schneider (Basel), and Charles Baker (London).
The report characterizes sales to Wheeler, Beck, Ward and Schneider as commission sales; Baker's purchase is interpreted by Stevenson as probably intended for resale.
claims.grade: A++ for the four reported commission relationships pending direct primary verification; A for Baker resale interpretation

claims.claim: The Station stopped producing further microscopic preparations because sales did not cover costs.

secondary_extraction_pending_primary_ver.guard: These statements are useful locators and working extractions, but are not promoted to S until the German primary passage on pp. 130-131 is visually or textually checked.

trade_network_interpretation.mechanism: research station production → numbered catalogue commodity → bulk/commission sale to established microscope-slide and optical dealers → potential resale into dispersed private and institutional collections
trade_network_interpretation.significance: Naples preparations were not only direct research-station outputs. At least part of the commercial programme appears to have used existing dealer infrastructures, allowing a Station product number to circulate through a second commercial address layer.
trade_network_interpretation.comparison: This is structurally different from Cole's subscriber serial and Elcock's maker/dealer network: the producer is a research institution that attempts to monetize standardized microscopic preparations through external trade intermediaries.
trade_network_interpretation.claim_level: A++ mechanism pending primary dealer-table verification

archive_bridge.repository: Historical Archive of the Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn (ASZN)
archive_bridge.research_value: The archive categories are exactly those likely to retain order, invoice, dispatch, commission or dealer correspondence capable of turning the 1882-1884 sales summary into transaction-level histories.
archive_bridge.grade: S archive locator; contents of specific dealer files not yet inspected

named_archive_queries: mikroskopische Präparate / Präparaten-Verkauf / Commission / Rechnung / Versand / Bestellung / Copialettere 1882-1884
critical_guards: Do not attach St Andrews BPM/1/T8/6 or any other surviving copy to Wheeler, Beck, Ward, Schneider or Baker without individual-copy provenance.
Do not convert a catalogue offering number into a unique serial number; multiple physical copies could correspond to one offering.
Do not treat Baker as a documented commission reseller until the primary report wording is checked; Stevenson labels resale there as probable.
Do not assign post-1880 slides to Fritz Meyer merely from Naples provenance; Meyer died in 1880 and later Station production continued under other hands.
next: Visually inspect Mittheilungen Bd. 6 (1886), pp. 130-131 and transcribe the complete dealer-sales passage/table verbatim enough to close names, quantities, dates, commission wording and the profitability statement.
Then query ASZN correspondence/copybooks/accounts for the five named dealers, starting with Wheeler February 1882 because quantity and month are already bounded.
Only after transaction records are found, compare dealer stock catalogues/labels to surviving Naples slides for resale traces.
